prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks, opening a new regime of precision measurement of time and frequency

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B014 as a single-achievement prize for Katori and Ye. After the full first-round exchange the case rests on three things I can state without counting support. First, the invention is conceptually distinct: the magic-wavelength lattice removes the light shift so that many neutral atoms sit in the Lamb-Dicke regime, with Doppler and recoil shifts suppressed and quantum projection noise reduced at the same time. That is a different principle from the single trapped ion, so it is not a refinement of the 2012 work. Second, it is experimentally verified in the way the committee requires: independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE, NIST) reproduce and compare clocks at about 1e-18. Third, the door it opens has already been used: centimetre-scale gravitational redshift, bounds on drifting constants and dark-matter searches are in the literature, so the prize would reward an invention with measured consequences. The credit is a clear pair, concept and first demonstration (Katori) and record realisation (Ye). The chair rightly notes that agreement on B014 is partly movement towards it. I therefore tested it against my own criterion, who did the original experiment, and not against the count, and it still stands. My citation says invention and realisation, and it deliberately avoids implying credit for the whole clock community.
statement.case_against: The honest reservations are the ones all six supporters share, and I weigh them as follows. Overlap with the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes is real as a prize lineage, but I do not think it defeats B014, because the new element is the neutral-atom lattice principle and not the frequency counting or the ion control. The unfinished SI redefinition is a regulatory consequence, not a condition of the invention. The priority question is the one I cannot close: Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow, Takamoto and the ion-clock groups are outside the two names, and the dates for the magic-wavelength proposal (2001-2003) and the first strontium demonstrations are recalled, not checked by me. I would want an expert check of those dates before the final ballot, and if they showed that Katori's priority does not hold, I would reconsider the pairing. A further caution is that B042, my opening first choice, is in my own field. I have discounted it for that reason and for the missing STEM-corrector originators.

responses.point: The Chair asks Lindroth whether the lattice clock is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes in a way a citation can state in one sentence. Lindroth argues it gives a new physical result, centimetre-scale gravitational redshift and constraints on constants, and not only better resolution, and she keeps the invention and realisation wording.
responses.response: I support her answer and would build the citation on it. One sentence can carry the distinction: the invention is trapping many neutral atoms at the magic wavelength so that the clock transition is unperturbed, and the realisation is the 1e-18 performance. That separates the work from the comb, which counts optical cycles, and from ion control, which uses one ion. Where I still ask for more than she says is the chronology: as the person closest to the field she is best placed to confirm the 2001-2003 proposal dates and the first demonstrations, because her file and mine both say we recalled them. If the dates hold, I think the distinction can be defended.

responses.point: Danielsson prefers B021 (IceCube) because nature supplied a diffuse flux of TeV-PeV neutrinos nobody could have predicted, he ranks the clock fifth as an instrument, and he concedes that confirmation outside IceCube is thin and that the three-name credit is somewhat arbitrary.
responses.response: I accept that discovery from nature carries real weight, and I agree that the flux is far above five sigma in several IceCube channels. My difficulty is the standard I apply: I want to be absolutely sure we have identified the people who did the original work, and for B021 the Baikal, AMANDA and DUMAND lineage and the leaders of a very large collaboration make three names a choice and not a finding. Confirmation by other detectors is also not yet there. I would not call the clock only an instrument, because it has already produced measurements of nature (gravitational redshift over centimetres, bounds on constants). I would keep B021 as a serious later candidate. A concrete fact that would change my view is an expert historical note that supports a specific three-name set, together with KM3NeT or Baikal-GVD reaching comparable sensitivity.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B016 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) as a new class of matter defined by topology, with theory and the HgTe experiment in one prize, and says B014 is the cleaner configuration if the committee finds the credit gap too large. He also asked me whether the three B042 names can stand alone.
responses.response: On B042, I answer him directly: no, not with confidence. Rose, Haider and Urban cover the TEM corrector, and Krivanek's STEM corrector is a parallel, independently confirmed branch outside the names, so I would not defend those three as the full original work. On B016, I agree with him that the scientific case is strong and that Molenkamp's HgTe observation is the original experiment. But the HgTe proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the three-dimensional topological insulator work both lie outside the names, Zhang has died, and the 2016 prize covers the topological theme. He himself calls B014 the cleaner configuration. Given my criterion of naming the people who did the original work, I take that concession as decisive and keep B016 below B014.

responses.point: Kroll prefers B014 and says his metrology bias should be discounted. He asks the committee to test whether it would rank the clock first on conceptual weight and not on measurement precision, and he proposes a single-achievement prize because a B014 plus single-person B008 part breaks the three-person limit.
responses.response: I agree with the single-achievement framing. I do not see a clean second part that fits with two clock names under the three-person limit, so adding one would only blur the credit. On his conceptual-weight test, I think the clock passes: it changes which measurements can be made, and the weight is in the magic-wavelength principle and the Lamb-Dicke regime, not in the number of digits. His bias toward metrology is a fair warning, so I weigh the independent reproduction across laboratories more than his enthusiasm. I also keep my round-1 position that the SI redefinition should not be a precondition.

uncertainties: Exact priority dates for Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and the first strontium lattice-clock demonstrations, and the claims of Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow and Takamoto, are recalled and not verified by me; an expert check is needed before the final ballot.
Whether the committee accepts the lattice clock as distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, a judgement on which colleagues with field knowledge differ in emphasis.
Whether the unfinished SI redefinition of the second makes recognition early. I think it does not, but I cannot rule out that colleagues weigh it more heavily.

For the alternatives: whether B017 is early given the unsettled pairing mechanism and sample variability, and whether B042 can be credited without Krivanek and whether physics or chemistry is its natural home.
statement.conflict_note: Field connection: B042 (aberration-corrected electron optics) is in my own field of transmission electron microscopy at Chalmers. I ranked it first in the opening ballot, I list it only as an alternative, and I would recuse myself from the final decision on B042 or ask colleagues to test my judgement. Göran Johansson is a Chalmers colleague and B009 (circuit QED) is his community, but no personal tie affects my view of B014 or B009. I have no specific conflict for B014, B017, B016, B021, B008, B018, B020 or B001. I am not recusing on B014, and my first-round preference for it was formed on my own reading, not on the count.
